summary: Eleanor Nesbitt is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She studied at Girton College, Cambridge (~1969–1972) and the University of Oxford (~1972–1973), and later served as emerita professor in Education Studies at the University of Warwick (~1989).

Eleanor Rosch is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned a bachelor's at Reed College and a Ph.D. at Harvard under Roger Brown. Her academic posts include Connecticut College, Brown University, and UC Berkeley from 1971.

Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a Tibetologist who studied East Asian History at Sapienza University of Rome under Luciano Petech (~1966–1971). She held posts at the University of Bonn and Sapienza University of Rome as Associate Professor from 1980.
Elena France Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned her Doctor of Philosophy at Harvard University under the supervision of Charles Hallisey.

Elena Mucciarelli is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Tübingen. She held positions at the University of Tübingen (2016–2017) and the University of Groningen (2020) as Assistant Professor and Gonda Lecturer.

Eli Franco works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at Tel Aviv, EHESS, Paris Nanterre/EPHE under Charles Malamoud, and Hamburg, he held posts at Kyoto, La Trobe, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Vienna, and Leipzig University (2004–2021).

Elijah Sacvan Ary is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University (~2001–2007) under supervisors Janet Gyatso and Leonard van der Kuijp, as well as Charles Hallisey and Geshe Karma Sonam.

Eliot Deutsch was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Wisconsin-Madison, Chicago, Harvard, and Columbia (Ph.D. 1956–1960). He held posts at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and the University of Hawaiʻi (1967–2006).

Elisa Freschi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed doctoral studies under Raffaele Torella (~2002–2006). She has held posts at Sapienza University of Rome, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Vienna University, and IKGA (~2017–2022).

Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza is a religious studies scholar who studied at Würzburg and Münster. She held professorships at the University of Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and Harvard University from 1988.

Elizabeth A. Cecil is a scholar in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. Educated at Hastings College, Tennessee, and Brown under James L. Fitzgerald, she held posts at Groningen, Leiden (~2016–2018), and Florida State University (~2018).

Elizabeth Anne Morrison is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed her doctoral studies under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt, and held teaching posts at Amherst College (1998–1999) and Middlebury College (attested 2008).

Elizabeth De Michelis is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from SOAS and the University of Cambridge (~1998–2002). She held posts at Cambridge as director in 2000 and at the University of Oxford's theology faculty.

Elizabeth English is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Oxford by 1999 under doctoral supervisor Alexis Sanderson, also studying with Harunaga Isaacson.

Elizabeth Errington is a historian and archaeologist specializing in Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS under Adrian David Hugh Bivar and held posts at the Fitzwilliam Museum, the British Institute of Persian Studies, Oxford, and the British Museum (1993).

Elizabeth Guthrie is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Canterbury in 1994. She served as a tutor in Religious Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2007).

Elizabeth J. Harris is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her doctorate (~1988–1993) from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and Kelaniya under Ananda Guruge and Y. Karunadasa, later working at Birmingham (~2014).

Elizabeth J. Perry is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Michigan (~1969–1978). She held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1978–1990) and Harvard University (~1997).

Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Virginia under supervisor Paul Groner. She served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).
Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who founded Theology & Sexuality and was appointed director at the University of Winchester in 2021.
